believed_cause: checkoutservice's PlaceOrder path repeatedly opens and fully parses /src/log.csv ten times per order, and the resulting file-I/O and CPU-heavy CSV parsing drive CPU CFS throttling and severe latency.
lesson: For CPU-saturation symptoms, include excessive file reads as a supported code-level CPU cause and do not attribute pod_cpu_overload until source inspection excludes busy loops, artificial delays, and repeated or unbounded file I/O. File-I/O-driven parsing can present as CPU throttling even when there is no active spin-wait.
summary: Added a confirm_excessive_file_reads_code branch to the CPU saturation SOP and updated triage and attribution so file-read-driven CPU pressure is excluded before pod_cpu_overload is assigned.

believed_cause: A busy-wait loop in checkoutservice's PlaceOrder request path spins roughly 500ms per call, consuming CPU and producing the observed CPU saturation, CFS throttling, and ~750ms latency response.
lesson: When CPU throttling and latency rise together with a normal CPU limit and no error logs, source inspection must precede any pod_cpu_overload or limit-misconfiguration attribution; a loop that spins/checks an elapsed-time condition is a CPU-consuming busy loop and should be classified code_busy_loop, not code_artificial_delay, when the CPU rise and throttling corroborate it.
summary: Rewrote confirm_busy_loop_code to treat an elapsed-time spin loop as a CPU-consuming busy loop and to use CPU-rise/throttling evidence to distinguish it from a non-CPU blocking artificial delay, and reinforced source triage before pod_cpu_overload attribution.

believed_cause: Pod-level network delay on ts-price-service caused the externally observed latency, which propagated to upstream services such as ts-basic-service and ts-gateway-service while pods stayed healthy and application logs showed no internal errors.
lesson: When latency alerts span multiple services, use service dependencies to find the deepest downstream root instead of picking the largest relative spike alone, and compare pod placement to rule out node_network_delay. Also use tight controller-to-service timestamps and absence of error logs to separate network delay from code_artificial_delay.
summary: Updated the latency SOP to use dependency direction and pod-node placement to select the downstream root and distinguish pod_network_delay from node_network_delay, with explicit application-internal delay checks.

believed_cause: checkoutservice returns an unconditional fabricated 'charge card error' after a successful paymentservice Charge RPC, causing checkout HTTP 500s.
lesson: When a caller reports a downstream RPC failure but the downstream logs show the operation succeeded, suspect the caller's return/error construction (code_wrong_return) rather than the downstream service. Confirm by inspecting the caller's source and checking whether valid inputs reach a fabricated or unconditional error after the successful call.
summary: Updated application_request_or_response_failure to prioritize caller-side return/error construction when downstream success is observed and to strengthen code_wrong_return confirmation evidence.

believed_cause: Node-level network delay on worker-01 is the most likely root cause, though it should have been confirmed with an independent co-located workload rather than call-chain co-location alone.
lesson: Co-location of a delayed service with its callers is propagation evidence, not proof of node-wide network delay; require an independent co-located service with latency or network symptoms. Failed recent-log retrieval must not be treated as evidence that there is no application-internal delay.
summary: Revised service_latency_degradation to require independent node-wide evidence for node_network_delay, treat call-chain co-location as propagation, and handle unavailable recent logs without over-attributing.

believed_cause: Pod-level network delay on ts-seat-service caused the externally observed latency while pod health, application logs, and node placement stayed normal.
lesson: When attributing latency to pod_network_delay, do not rely on a single fast downstream-call log; explicitly compare caller-observed latency with server-side handler duration and the latency of the pod's own outbound dependency calls, and record code_artificial_delay as an alternative if internal handling gaps are seen.
summary: Revised the latency SOP to require comparing caller-observed latency with server-side handler duration and outbound dependency latency before confirming pod_network_delay and to record code_artificial_delay/downstream-delay alternatives.

believed_cause: The downstream ts-order-service pod was CPU-throttled, and calls from ts-inside-payment-service to it were slow; the agent incorrectly attributed the caller-side latency to pod_network_delay without measuring outbound call latency.
lesson: When latency alerts include a CPU CFS throttle on a downstream dependency, treat pod_cpu_overload as a primary competing root cause and measure the caller's outbound-call latency to that dependency; fast handler logs inside the throttled pod do not exclude CPU scheduling or queueing delay. Also treat an inbound traffic surge as possible retry amplification until proven otherwise.
summary: Added explicit CPU-saturation and traffic-surge investigation plus a pod_cpu_overload confirmation step, and tightened pod_network_delay attribution to require excluding CPU throttling on the call path and measuring outbound dependency latency.

believed_cause: The ts-route-service Deployment uses dnsPolicy None with an unreachable custom nameserver 10.255.11.254, causing pod-local DNS resolution failures for both tsdb-mysql-leader and istiod and leading to CrashLoopBackOff.
lesson: For a single pod with DNS errors, confirm pod-local DNS misconfiguration by checking dnsPolicy/dnsConfig, verifying that target Services exist, and comparing same-node pods. A dnsPolicy None with an unreachable custom nameserver explains failures resolving both business dependencies and istiod and should exclude node-wide network packet loss.
summary: Expanded the DNS branch of pod_crash_or_restart to require checking dnsPolicy/dnsConfig, target Service existence, and same-node pod health to confirm pod-local DNS misconfiguration and exclude node network loss.

believed_cause: worker-01 has a high-magnitude TCP retransmission spike while hosting most latency-affected services, with healthy kube-proxy and containerd, indicating node-level packet loss.
lesson: A node-aligned TCP retransmission spike with multiple affected services placed on the same node is sufficient to support node_network_packet_loss; clean application error logs do not refute it. Do not classify such a case as node_network_delay when the retransmission increase is meaningful.
summary: Clarified packet-loss confirmation to rely on node-aligned retransmission evidence and explicitly stated that clean application logs do not refute packet loss, while steering high-retransmission cases away from node_network_delay.

believed_cause: The recommendationservice Service exposes port and targetPort 8080 as UDP while the application and its gRPC probes expect TCP, so TCP/gRPC client traffic to the Service is not routed.
lesson: When pods and endpoints are healthy but a Service is unreachable, compare the Service port and targetPort protocols (TCP/UDP) with the container listener and client/probe protocol; a numeric port match can still be a protocol mismatch. Treat gRPC/HTTP probes as TCP evidence and classify a UDP Service for a TCP workload as service_protocol_mismatch, not targetPort mismatch.
summary: Strengthened routing inspection and protocol-confirmation steps so UDP-vs-TCP mismatch is explicitly separated from targetPort and selector mismatches, including partial service unreachability.

believed_cause: productcatalogservice clears the required product ID (productID = empty string) before lookup, causing NotFound responses for valid product requests.
lesson: When a caller supplies a valid request value but the reachable callee returns a semantic missing or empty-parameter error, inspect the callee's request-handling source before attributing the defect to the caller. A downstream NotFound naming an empty ID can be code_missing_parameter inside the callee.
summary: Updated the request-failure SOP to route reachable-callee semantic missing or empty-parameter errors into callee source inspection and to clarify that a callee clearing a valid required ID is code_missing_parameter.

believed_cause: CPU CFS throttling from expensive order-query processing on ts-order-service caused its latency to propagate to ts-preserve-service and upstream callers, while the sharp ts-contacts-service spike was a secondary alternative rather than the primary root.
lesson: When a CPU CFS throttle alert names a downstream service on the caller's call path, confirm caller-side outbound-call latency to that service before preferring a different leaf service's larger latency spike; fast leaf handler logs do not make a leaf spike the root while call-path CPU saturation is unresolved.
summary: Added explicit prioritization and confirmation rules for CPU CFS-throttled call-path dependencies, requiring caller-side outbound-call latency comparison before attributing latency to another leaf service or network delay.

believed_cause: frontend chooseAd creates a temporary CSV and writes 30,000 rows per ad-selection request, causing the filesystem write surge, elevated CPU, and downstream 503 performance degradation.
lesson: A large fixed per-request file write can produce both a filesystem-write surge and CPU/latency degradation, even when pods are healthy and some requests still return 200. Inspect request-path source for temp-file creation and bulk row writes before attributing the CPU signal to a generic busy loop or pod CPU overload.
summary: Strengthened service_latency_or_io_degradation so per-request large file writes are treated as code_excessive_file_writes even when accompanied by CPU elevation or 503s.

believed_cause: The ts-food-service Deployment sets dnsPolicy None with custom nameserver 10.255.18.254, which cannot resolve tsdb-mysql-leader or istiod, causing CrashLoopBackOff.
lesson: When a single pod crashes with MySQL connection-initialization errors, inspect the root exception for UnknownHostException or name-resolution failure before pursuing MySQL credentials or port mismatch; dnsPolicy None with an unreachable custom nameserver and failures resolving both business and Istio names indicate pod-local DNS misconfiguration.
summary: Added an explicit DNS/name-resolution branch from MySQL startup-crash inspection and reinforced capturing UnknownHostException evidence before MySQL credential or port checks.

believed_cause: A transient checkoutservice pod startup/rollout gap caused frontend's gRPC connection to be refused; current endpoints and subsequent orders were healthy, so the code_missing_parameter conclusion was unsupported.
lesson: When a connection-refused/reset error aligns with a recent callee pod start or rollout and the callee later succeeds, treat it as transient startup connectivity loss rather than a code-level missing parameter. Application source inspection must not override live connectivity and callee success evidence.
summary: Added a transient startup/rollout connectivity-gap confirmation branch and guidance to avoid misattributing connection-refused errors to code_missing_parameter.

believed_cause: The checkoutservice PlaceOrder handler repeatedly opens and reads the full /src/log.csv 10 times per request, creating CPU-heavy parsing work that causes CPU throttling and severe latency.
lesson: When CPU throttling and severe latency occur with a normal CPU limit, healthy pods, no error logs, and request-path source that repeatedly reads/parses a file, classify code_excessive_file_reads rather than pod_cpu_overload or code_busy_loop.
summary: Clarified that fixed repeated per-request file reads are sufficient evidence for code_excessive_file_reads and must be preferred over pod_cpu_overload or a busy-loop diagnosis when they explain CPU throttling and latency.

believed_cause: A request-path busy-wait in frontend chooseAd spins until about 800ms elapse, causing CPU saturation/CFS throttling and severe latency; downstream ad DeadlineExceeded logs are secondary.
lesson: Duration-bounded spin-waits in request handlers such as chooseAd are code_busy_loop, not pod_cpu_overload or code_artificial_delay; inspect the handler file identified during triage rather than assuming main.go, and treat downstream timeout logs as secondary when the caller spins.
summary: Updated confirm_busy_loop_code to inspect the triaged handler file, recognize fixed-duration request-path spins like chooseAd, and treat downstream DeadlineExceeded as secondary; added matching signals and triage guidance.

believed_cause: Application-level busy processing in ts-order-service, such as heavy getSoldTickets or large result-set work, consumed CPU and caused CFS throttling that propagated latency upstream; this should be classified as code_busy_loop rather than pod_cpu_overload.
lesson: A CPU CFS throttle on a call-path dependency does not by itself prove pod_cpu_overload. Inspect the throttled service's logs for repeated business-method work, large result-set processing, or tight-loop behavior, and label code_busy_loop when application code is the CPU consumer rather than stopping at pod_cpu_overload.
summary: Added code_busy_loop as a CPU-saturation root candidate and a terminal branch that distinguishes application busy processing from external pod CPU overload.

believed_cause: An active request-path spin-wait in checkoutservice PlaceOrder consumes CPU until about 500ms elapses, causing CPU saturation and latency degradation.
lesson: A fixed-duration request-path loop that actively checks elapsed time is code_busy_loop, not code_artificial_delay or generic pod_cpu_overload, when CPU throttling and latency align with the spin. The SOP should explicitly cover checkoutservice PlaceOrder-style 500ms elapsed-time spins and prevent competing top predictions once active spinning is confirmed.
summary: Added explicit guidance and confirmation criteria for checkoutservice PlaceOrder fixed-duration elapsed-time spin-waits as code_busy_loop, excluding artificial-delay and pod-overload alternatives once active spinning is confirmed.

believed_cause: checkoutservice PlaceOrder creates /tmp/tmp.csv and writes 60,000 CSV records per request, causing excessive filesystem writes and the observed CPU saturation.
lesson: When CPU saturation co-occurs with a filesystem-write surge, inspect request-path file creation and bulk writes before attributing the incident to pod_cpu_overload or code_busy_loop. Large per-request temp-file or CSV writes are code_excessive_file_writes and can explain both the fs_write_bytes spike and raised CPU.
summary: Added filesystem-write-surge signals and a confirm_excessive_file_writes_code branch to the CPU-saturation SOP, and required excluding file-write work before attributing CPU overload or a busy loop.

believed_cause: An explicit blocking time.Sleep(3000ms) in productcatalogservice's ListProducts handler added a fixed artificial delay, causing productcatalogservice latency and downstream frontend and recommendationservice slow responses.
lesson: When pods are healthy and a shared service plus its callers show severe fixed-duration latency with no application error logs, inspect request-handler and helper source files, not only main.go, for an active non-zero blocking sleep; a fixed sleep matching observed latency is code_artificial_delay rather than busy-loop or excessive-file-read defect.
summary: Updated service_latency_or_io_degradation to route healthy fixed-duration latency to request-handler/helper source inspection and to confirm blocking time.Sleep artificial delays outside main.go with duration alignment.

believed_cause: The CPU-throttled ts-order-service was doing excessive application work (code_busy_loop), though the diagnosis should have explicitly reconciled the parallel ts-basic/ts-route latency branch before finalizing.
lesson: Trace the full transitive call path to a CPU-throttled service, such as ts-travel-service -> ts-seat-service -> ts-order-service, and require caller-observed latency to it plus busy-code logs. Do not let a CPU-throttled dependency on one branch explain away latency alerts on a parallel branch; record any unexplained parallel branch as a separate candidate or show retry amplification.
summary: Added transitive call-path tracing for CPU-throttled services and a requirement to reconcile parallel-branch latency alerts before confirming code_busy_loop.

believed_cause: The frontend productHandler extracts the product ID from the request path and then explicitly clears it to an empty string before validation, causing valid /product/{id} requests to be rejected as 'product id not specified' with HTTP 400.
lesson: When a handler reports a required request parameter missing despite a valid value being present in the path or query, inspect the handler's extraction and validation code for an explicit clear, overwrite, nil assignment, or defaulting before validation, and classify it as code_missing_parameter rather than code_wrong_return or a downstream fault.
summary: Revised application_request_or_response_failure to explicitly cover local HTTP handlers that clear an extracted valid path/query parameter before validation, producing a missing-parameter error while the original request contained a valid value.

believed_cause: Repeated OOMKilled in shippingservice indicates memory growth in its code, likely code_memory_leak, not an independently too-low 128Mi limit.
lesson: An ordinary finite limit such as 128Mi plus OOMKilled is not evidence of container_memory_limit_too_low, and memory_capacity_mismatch is not an OOM root cause. Before concluding, inspect shippingservice source for unbounded allocation/retention or repeated file reads; if source inspection is not done, report the code-level cause as unconfirmed rather than ranking low limit first.
summary: Strengthened the OOM SOP: 128Mi is ordinary, source inspection is mandatory before low-limit attribution, and memory_capacity_mismatch is excluded from OOM conclusions.

believed_cause: checkoutservice PlaceOrder repeatedly opened and ReadAll-ed /src/log.csv ten times per request, creating CPU-heavy file-read work that caused CPU saturation, CFS throttling, and severe latency while pods stayed healthy.
lesson: A fixed number of repeated request-path file reads can be the concrete CPU-demand mechanism; once source confirms it, conclude code_excessive_file_reads and do not rank pod_cpu_overload or code_busy_loop as competing top predictions.
summary: Added explicit confirmation guidance that repeated request-path file reads are the sole supported CPU root cause and must not be ranked alongside pod_cpu_overload or code_busy_loop.

believed_cause: An artificial delay in paymentservice's RPC response path, likely a Node.js setTimeout/Promise delay after the charge business logic, makes successful charges return about 2 seconds late.
lesson: Artificial-delay confirmation must cover non-blocking JavaScript timers and delayed gRPC callbacks, not just blocking sleeps; fast business logs do not prove network delay. Also do not attribute to pod_network_delay by exclusion alone without positive pod-level network evidence and co-located-service comparison.
summary: Updated the artificial-delay branch to include Node.js setTimeout/Promise response deferral and tightened pod_network_delay attribution so fast business logs or code exclusion alone are insufficient.

believed_cause: ts-order-service is running a code_busy_loop: repeated getSoldTickets and large-result-set processing under CPU CFS throttling makes order calls slow and propagates latency to ts-preserve and its parallel branches; ts-basic is more likely retry/load propagation than an independently confirmed pod_network_delay.
lesson: Confirm code_busy_loop only when busy-processing logs in the CPU-throttled dependency are paired with slow caller-observed outbound latency to that dependency; do not rank a fast-handler parallel branch as pod_network_delay unless caller-side outbound latency to that branch is slow and retry amplification from the slow caller is excluded.
summary: Added guidance to require caller-outbound latency before confirming code_busy_loop and to treat fast-handler parallel branches as possible retry-amplification propagation rather than default pod_network_delay candidates.

believed_cause: quote.go's CreateQuoteFromCount -> CreateQuoteFromFloat creates /tmp/tmp.csv and writes 30,000 CSV rows on every GetQuote request, producing the filesystem-write surge and the accompanying CPU elevation.
lesson: CPU saturation co-occurring with a filesystem-write surge on a healthy service with fast, error-free request logs is a per-request file-write code defect, not overload or a busy loop; once source shows the bulk write, conclude code_excessive_file_writes alone instead of keeping code_busy_loop or pod_cpu_overload as competing predictions.
summary: Added a signal for a generic performance-degradation symptom whose alert is CPU saturation plus a filesystem-write surge, recorded the shippingservice quote.go 30,000-row /tmp/tmp.csv per-request write pattern, and required confirm_excessive_file_writes_code to be concluded alone with busy-loop and pod_cpu_overload explicitly excluded as competing predictions.

believed_cause: Node network packet loss on worker-02 is the leading root cause, evidenced by a high-magnitude TCP retransmission spike on the node hosting all latency-affected services while kube-proxy and containerd remain healthy.
lesson: When all latency-affected services are colocated on a node with a high-magnitude TCP retransmission spike and healthy node components, conclude node_network_packet_loss; do not keep node_network_delay as a competing top prediction or elevate a different node with only a minor retransmission increase.
summary: Strengthened packet-loss confirmation so colocated affected services plus a high-magnitude TCP retransmission spike confirm packet loss, refute delay, and prevent unrelated nodes from being ranked as top causes.

believed_object: app/shippingservice (quote.go GetQuote helper path CreateQuoteFromCount -> CreateQuoteFromFloat)
believed_cause: Every GetQuote request creates a temporary CSV and writes ~30000 rows, so request-path file work (not network delay) explains the multi-second p90 latency while the handler's business logs still show instant received/completed.
lesson: A partial read of a helper file (only the Quote struct in quote.go) is not evidence of absence of a defect, and fast business logs plus healthy pods do not establish pod_network_delay: quote/pricing helpers reachable from the hot RPC must be retrieved in full and checked for per-request temp-file or bulk writes before any network root cause is concluded.
summary: Strengthened source triage and the excessive-file-write confirmation so a leaf service with instant business logs and a partially-inspected quote helper is driven to code_excessive_file_writes (shippingservice quote.go per-request 30000-row temp CSV) instead of pod_network_delay.

believed_cause: The kubelet service on worker-01 is inactive/dead, making pods on that node such as redis-cart unreachable and causing cartservice/frontend connection failures.
lesson: When a Service selector, ports, and endpoints are correct but connectivity to a Running endpoint fails, check the endpoint node kubelet through log-retrieval/API errors and CheckNodeServiceStatus; an inactive kubelet with node status Unknown is kubelet_unavailable, not node packet loss or delay.
summary: Added an endpoint-node kubelet health inspection and confirmation branch to service_connectivity_or_routing_failure so correct Service config plus failed endpoint connectivity and kubelet:10250 log errors lead to kubelet_unavailable rather than network causes.

believed_cause: Frontend's addToCart handler passed userID and productID in swapped positions to cartservice, corrupting cart identifiers and causing intermittent availability errors/HTTP 503s while pods remained healthy.
lesson: When multiple frontend journeys return 503 with healthy pods, inspect downstream callee logs for semantically swapped identifiers; a cartservice log showing a product ID in userId and a session UUID in productId is strong evidence of a caller argument-order defect, so confirm the caller's cart/insert call site before considering missing-parameter or wrong-return causes.
summary: Added signals, localization evidence, and wrong-argument-order confirmation guidance for healthy-pod frontend 503s caused by swapped userID/productID arguments observed in downstream cartservice logs.

believed_cause: frontend setCurrencyHandler repeatedly opens and reads /src/log.csv ten times per request, causing CPU saturation, CFS throttling, high latency, and secondary downstream adservice DeadlineExceeded warnings.
lesson: When frontend CPU throttling and latency coexist with downstream adservice DeadlineExceeded logs, inspect frontend request handlers such as setCurrencyHandler for repeated file reads and treat the downstream timeout as secondary. Once code_excessive_file_reads is confirmed, do not keep code_busy_loop or pod_cpu_overload as competing top predictions.
summary: Added the frontend setCurrencyHandler repeated /src/log.csv read signal and strengthened the rule to report code_excessive_file_reads as the single leading cause without competing busy-loop or pod-overload predictions.

believed_cause: The shippingservice GetQuote request path creates and writes a large per-request temporary CSV, adding seconds of latency to checkoutservice PlaceOrder while pods remain healthy.
lesson: A source response that stops at the shippingservice Quote type declaration does not exclude the known per-request 30000-row temp-file write, and a claimed checkoutservice getUserCart time.Sleep must be visibly present in retrieved source before code_artificial_delay is confirmed. Fully retrieve request-path helper bodies before excluding code_excessive_file_writes.
summary: Strengthened latency source triage to require full shippingservice quote.go and checkoutservice handler retrieval, reject unverified time.Sleep claims from truncated excerpts, and keep code_excessive_file_writes as the leading checkoutservice PlaceOrder latency explanation until the shippingservice write site is actually excluded.

believed_cause: productcatalogservice ListProducts repeatedly opens and reads /src/log.csv 15 times per request, while the time.Sleep(extraLatency) hook is dormant because EXTRA_LATENCY is unset, producing severe latency and downstream frontend failures.
lesson: When latency is severe and source shows repeated request-path file reads, conclude code_excessive_file_reads as the single leading cause; a sleep whose environment variable is unset is dormant and must not be retained as artificial delay, and pod_network_delay is excluded once the file-read work explains the latency.
summary: Added an explicit excessive-file-reads branch for productcatalogservice ListProducts and tightened artificial-delay and network-delay exclusions when EXTRA_LATENCY is unset.

believed_cause: Pod-level network delay on ts-contacts-service is the most likely cause: it is the deepest alerted leaf with extreme latency and throughput drop, healthy pods, fast server-side entry processing, no CPU-throttle alert, and no application errors, while upstream services show propagated latency; node-wide delay is not independently supported.
lesson: For a leaf latency candidate, confirm pod_network_delay only when caller-side logs show the outbound call itself is slow while the leaf's server-side handler completion is fast; same-timestamp entry logs and same-node co-location are not enough. Do not rank node_network_delay unless an independent co-located workload outside the call chain is degraded.
summary: Strengthened the latency SOP with leaf-service caller-observed latency requirements and a guardrail against ranking node_network_delay from call-chain co-location alone.

believed_cause: A code-level artificial delay in ts-security-service is the most likely cause, but the conclusion should have been conditional because caller-side outbound timing and server-side handler duration were not obtained.
lesson: TCP connect success and empty application logs do not prove code_artificial_delay or exclude pod_network_delay; for a hang at a downstream call boundary, measure caller-observed outbound latency and target handler duration, trace the target's downstream dependencies, and keep the cause conditional if that evidence is missing.
summary: Added a hung-downstream call-boundary measurement and code_artificial_delay confirmation step, and warned that TCP reachability or missing logs are not timing evidence.

believed_cause: The namespace storage quota hard limit of 1Gi blocks creation of the declared 2Gi redis-cart PVC, so the PVC is absent and redis-cart remains Pending.
lesson: When a Pending pod reports a referenced PVC not found and the PVC inventory is empty, compare the workload's declared PVC storage request with the namespace ResourceQuota hard limit; a request larger than the hard limit blocks PVC creation even when quota usage is zero. Do not treat zero quota usage as proof quota is not blocking, and do not route to PV binding compatibility until an actual PVC exists.
summary: Updated pending_pod_storage_dependency to route missing referenced PVCs to namespace storage-quota confirmation and to compare the declared PVC request with the quota hard limit instead of treating zero usage as non-blocking.

believed_cause: worker-01 kubelet is inactive/dead, making the node Unknown/NotReady and preventing the nodeSelector-constrained paymentservice pod from scheduling.
lesson: When a Pending pod is pinned to a node that is Unknown/NotReady and the node kubelet is inactive, treat kubelet_unavailable as the root cause; unreachable or unschedulable taints are consequences, not taint/toleration mismatches, and node_network_packet_loss should not be ranked without node-aligned retransmission evidence.
summary: Added routing and exclusion guidance so a Pending pod pinned to an Unknown/NotReady node with inactive kubelet is attributed to kubelet_unavailable rather than taint mismatch or packet loss.

believed_cause: The redis-cart datastore pod was CPU-saturated and CFS-throttled, which slowed cartservice's Redis operations and propagated as latency to checkoutservice and frontend while all application pods stayed healthy and error-free.
lesson: When latency increases across a dependency chain (cartservice/checkoutservice/frontend) and the only resource anomaly is CPU saturation/throttling on a downstream datastore such as redis-cart, conclude pod_cpu_overload on that datastore and treat the upstream latency as propagation; do not require application source for a datastore and do not keep upstream app pod_cpu_overload or node_network_delay as competing predictions without independent evidence.
summary: Added datastore-CPU-throttling signals (e.g., redis-cart throttling under caller latency) and a confirm_datastore_cpu_overload branch, and clarified that a source-less backend datastore's CPU overload is the root cause while upstream latency is propagation.

believed_cause: checkoutservice PlaceOrder repeatedly opens and reads /src/log.csv ten times per request, causing CPU saturation, CFS throttling, and multi-second latency.
lesson: When source confirms repeated request-path file reads as the concrete CPU-consuming mechanism, the conclusion must be code_excessive_file_reads alone; pod_cpu_overload and code_busy_loop must not be ranked or retained as competing top predictions. For checkoutservice, a fixed-count PlaceOrder loop that opens and ReadAll-s /src/log.csv ten times per request is file-read work, not a busy-loop.
summary: Updated service_cpu_or_resource_saturation so checkoutservice PlaceOrder repeated /src/log.csv reads are explicitly classified as code_excessive_file_reads and pod_cpu_overload and code_busy_loop are excluded from the top predictions once that mechanism is confirmed.

believed_cause: checkoutservice convertCurrency clears the target currency before calling currencyservice, producing mismatched currency codes and a panic/HTTP 500 during PlaceOrder.
lesson: When checkout returns HTTP 500 with a mismatching-currency-codes panic and payment/email traffic vanishes, inspect checkoutservice currency conversion for a cleared target currency and classify it as code_missing_parameter, not checkoutservice or currencyservice wrong_return.
summary: Added checkoutservice mismatching-currency panic signals and guidance to confirm a cleared target currency as code_missing_parameter while excluding wrong_return and currencyservice attribution.

believed_cause: frontend productHandler extracts the valid product ID from the /product/{id} path and then clears it before validation, causing HTTP 400 product id not specified and preventing downstream calls.
lesson: A local handler that extracts a valid path parameter and then clears it before validation is code_missing_parameter; recommendationservice availability missing is secondary, and code_wrong_return must not be ranked for frontend or recommendationservice.
summary: Added explicit frontend product-detail 400 guidance to the local-handler missing-parameter branch and forbade code_wrong_return or recommendationservice attribution as competing top predictions.

believed_cause: The checkoutservice target currency is cleared or overwritten to empty before convertCurrency or the currencyservice call, so PlaceOrder combines Money values with mismatching currency codes and panics.
lesson: For checkoutservice HTTP 500 with panic mismatching currency codes, inspect the actual target currency passed to convertCurrency and classify a cleared or empty currency as code_missing_parameter; do not infer code_wrong_argument_order from userID/userCurrency variable ordering, a truncated source excerpt, or blame currencyservice code_wrong_return.
summary: Strengthened the checkoutservice mismatching-currency-code guidance to require code_missing_parameter when the target currency is cleared or empty, reject wrong-argument-order conclusions based only on variable ordering or partial source, and exclude currencyservice wrong-return.

believed_cause: Multiple latency-anomalous TrainTicket services are co-located on worker-01 and include services outside ts-basic-service's downstream call chain, so a node-level network delay on worker-01 better explains the incident than pod-local delay on ts-basic-service.
lesson: When several latency-alerted services share a node, map whether they sit on parallel branches outside the selected leaf's call chain; such independent co-located anomalies favor node_network_delay. Do not confirm pod_network_delay for a leaf without caller-observed outbound latency and until node-wide impact is excluded.
summary: Strengthened the latency SOP to require node-placement mapping of all alerted services, treat parallel-branch co-located anomalies as independent node-wide evidence, prefer node_network_delay when such anomalies exist, and block pod_network_delay attribution without caller-observed outbound latency.

believed_cause: Repeated request-path reads of /src/log.csv 15 times per ListProducts request caused memory pressure and OOMKilled with an ordinary 128Mi limit, also producing severe latency; this is not a memory leak or a too-low memory limit.
lesson: When OOMKilled occurs with an ordinary finite limit such as 128Mi and source confirms repeated request-path file reads, conclude code_excessive_file_reads as the single leading root cause and do not rank code_memory_leak or container_memory_limit_too_low as competing top predictions.
summary: Revised the OOM SOP so confirmed repeated request-path file reads, including productcatalogservice ListProducts reading /src/log.csv 15 times per request, are the sole leading cause and exclude too-low-limit and memory-leak top predictions.

believed_cause: The paymentservice Kubernetes Service object is missing, so checkoutservice DNS lookup for paymentservice fails with 'no such host' and checkout cannot charge the card.
lesson: When a downstream DNS lookup fails with no such host, verify whether the target Service object exists; if it is absent while its pods are Running and Ready, classify it as a missing Service object and check namespace service quota, not as service_dns_resolution_failure, env-var address mismatch, or selector mismatch.
summary: Added explicit detection and confirmation that a DNS no-such-host failure with an absent downstream Service object is a missing_service_object creation failure, and made the quota check the final explanation check rather than allowing fallback to DNS/selector/config causes.

believed_cause: The frontend Deployment's CURRENCY_SERVICE_ADDR points at currencyservice:7001 while the currencyservice Service and container listen on 7000/TCP, so frontend calls fail with connection refused.
lesson: A connection refused to a downstream Service ClusterIP on a port not exposed by that Service, with healthy endpoints and matching Service targetPort/container port, is a caller-side address env-var mismatch, not a callee Service port mapping fault. Check the caller's downstream address env var for a wrong port and rank service_env_var_address_mismatch first.
summary: Broadened service_connectivity_or_routing_failure to recognize caller downstream address env var port mismatches and to exclude Service targetPort/container mapping faults when those ports agree.

believed_cause: checkoutservice PlaceOrder performs a huge per-request in-memory allocation loop that exhausts the 128Mi container limit and OOMKills the pod before downstream checkout calls complete.
lesson: A normal 128Mi limit should not be ranked as too low when source confirms a large allocation loop; confirm code_memory_leak as the single leading root cause and treat payment/email availability loss as secondary because checkoutservice crashes before calling them.
summary: Updated the OOM SOP to recognize a large per-request allocation loop in checkoutservice PlaceOrder as code_memory_leak, reject 128Mi low-limit and code_busy_loop as competing top predictions, and treat downstream payment/email availability loss as secondary.

believed_cause: frontend handlers.go chooseAd creates /tmp/tmp.csv and writes 30,000 CSV rows on every home-page and product-detail request, so that per-request bulk file write drives the fs_write_bytes surge, the CPU-side cost, and the HTTP 503s while every pod stays Running and Ready.
lesson: A frontend FILESYSTEM_WRITE_SURGE with CPU saturation, healthy pods, and no application error logs is a request-path bulk file-write defect, not pod_cpu_overload and not a busy loop; confirm it by reading the handler body that actually contains the temp-file create/write (e.g. chooseAd writing 30,000 rows to /tmp/tmp.csv), then report code_excessive_file_writes as the single leading root cause.
summary: Added frontend-specific signals, inspection actions and evidence for a chooseAd per-request 30,000-row /tmp/tmp.csv write, and forced code_excessive_file_writes to be the sole leading root cause with pod_cpu_overload and code_busy_loop excluded from the top predictions.

believed_cause: Productcatalogservice ListProducts repeatedly opens and reads /src/log.csv 15 times per request, driving CPU saturation/CFS throttling and latency; pod_cpu_overload is not the root cause.
lesson: Do not accept source excerpts that end at imports or before the handler body as proof that no repeated file-read defect exists; for productcatalogservice CPU/latency incidents, retrieve and inspect the full ListProducts body before attributing to pod_cpu_overload.
summary: Added productcatalogservice ListProducts /src/log.csv repeated-read guidance, required full source-body retrieval, and excluded pod_cpu_overload until repeated reads are ruled out.

believed_cause: The likely root cause was pod-level CPU overload/CFS throttling on ts-order-service; the code_busy_loop conclusion is unsupported because the retrieved logs do not contain large-result-set or tight-loop evidence.
lesson: Confirm code_busy_loop only when the retrieved logs explicitly show repeated busy work or large-result-set processing and caller-observed outbound latency to the throttled service is slow; a CPU CFS throttle with normal order-lookup logs should be recorded as pod_cpu_overload or left pending, not upgraded to code_busy_loop.
summary: Added evidence-quoting and guardrails so code_busy_loop is not confirmed from CPU throttle or normal order-lookup logs, and parallel-branch pod_network_delay requires caller-observed latency and retry exclusion.

believed_cause: containerd.service is inactive/dead on worker-01, so pod sandbox creation fails with a missing containerd socket and pods scheduled there remain stuck in Init:0/1.
lesson: When multiple pods on one node are stuck in Init:0/1 and events show FailedCreatePodSandBox with a missing or undialable containerd socket, check containerd once; if it is inactive/dead, conclude container_runtime_unavailable and do not rank kubelet_unavailable or node_network_delay as competing top predictions absent separate evidence.
summary: Revised pending_or_unschedulable_pod to route Init/ContainerCreating sandbox failures with containerd socket errors to container_runtime_unavailable and to exclude kubelet/network causes as competing top predictions without separate evidence.

believed_cause: productcatalogservice GetProduct returns NotFound for a valid product ID because its full lookup/return path incorrectly returns an error instead of the matched product.
lesson: When frontend product-detail 500s show productcatalogservice gRPC NotFound for a valid non-empty product ID, inspect GetProduct's full body for an incorrect NotFound return; recommendationservice availability loss is secondary, and a source excerpt ending at imports must not be used to confirm code_wrong_return.
summary: Added a productcatalogservice GetProduct NotFound/valid-ID branch that routes to code_wrong_return only after the full GetProduct body is retrieved, while excluding missing-parameter and frontend wrong-return attributions for this pattern.

believed_cause: The leading root cause is productcatalogservice code_excessive_file_reads in ListProducts (repeated /src/log.csv reads), not the unsupported claim that ListProducts creates /tmp/tmp.csv and writes 30,000 rows, since the retrieved source ended at imports.
lesson: A GetSourceCode response ending at imports is not evidence of a request-path write site. For productcatalogservice CPU or filesystem-write alerts, retrieve product_catalog.go and server.go fully and classify repeated /src/log.csv reads as code_excessive_file_reads; do not claim a temp CSV write unless the full ListProducts body shows it.
summary: Added explicit productcatalogservice guidance that imports-only source cannot support code_excessive_file_writes and that repeated /src/log.csv reads should be confirmed as code_excessive_file_reads.

believed_cause: The namespace CPU ResourceQuota cpu-quota is exhausted at requests.cpu 10/10, so the frontend ReplicaSet cannot create its pod, leaving the frontend Service with no endpoints.
lesson: When a Service has no endpoints because its deployment has zero ready replicas, inspect ReplicaSet FailedCreate events and ResourceQuota usage; a persistent exceeded quota event for requests.cpu should be concluded as namespace CPU quota exhaustion, not missing service account or deployment_zero_replicas. Treat empty endpoints and zero available replicas as consequences unless an independent persistent missing ServiceAccount failure is shown.
summary: Expanded workload-creation triage and quota confirmation to detect namespace CPU quota exhaustion from ReplicaSet FailedCreate exceeded quota events, and to exclude missing service account and zero-replica symptoms when quota exhaustion is persistent.

believed_cause: The GetQuote request path performs excessive per-request file writing in quote.go (CreateQuoteFromCount -> CreateQuoteFromFloat creating /tmp/tmp.csv with about 30000 rows), driving CPU saturation/CFS throttling and ~775-800ms latency; the busy-loop conclusion is unsupported because the retrieved quote.go excerpt ended at the Quote struct.
lesson: A shippingservice CPU/latency incident must not confirm code_busy_loop from a quote.go excerpt that ends at the Quote struct; retrieve CreateQuoteFromCount and CreateQuoteFromFloat fully. If they create a large per-request temp CSV, conclude code_excessive_file_writes as the single leading root cause and do not list pod_cpu_overload or code_artificial_delay as competing top predictions.
summary: Added a shippingservice quote.go truncation guard and routed it to full-body inspection and excessive-file-writes confirmation, excluding busy-loop, overload, and artificial-delay as competing top predictions once the write site is confirmed.

believed_cause: The frontend request-construction/RPC path clears the valid product ID to empty before calling productcatalogservice GetProduct, so GetProduct receives an empty ID and returns NotFound.
lesson: When a downstream NotFound reports an empty required ID while the original request path contained a valid ID, treat it as caller-side missing-parameter unless the full callee source shows it cleared the value; retrieve the full frontend handlers.go/rpc.go getProduct body before concluding, and do not accept an imports-only excerpt as evidence.
summary: Added handling for frontend product-detail HTTP 500 with downstream NotFound naming an empty product ID: inspect the full frontend rpc.go/getProduct request-construction path for a cleared ID, exclude productcatalogservice wrong-return when the ID arrived empty, and treat recommendationservice availability loss as secondary.

believed_cause: The frontend money helper's MultiplySlow performs an active per-request CPU busy-loop (reached from the cart/checkout path), raising frontend CPU into CFS throttling and lifting p50/p95 latency, while the 'clean' source review was based only on excerpts that ended at imports and never showed the function bodies.
lesson: A GetSourceCode response that ends at imports or package is not evidence that a file is clean; retrieve the full function bodies (e.g. frontend money/money.go MultiplySlow, or handlers/rpc/helper loops) before ruling out code-driven CPU, and never rank container_cpu_limit_too_low or pod_cpu_overload from imports-only excerpts when the limit is a normal 200m.
summary: Added frontend money/money.go MultiplySlow active busy-loop guidance and the rule that imports-only GetSourceCode excerpts are not proof of clean code, so frontend CPU saturation/latency is not misattributed to pod_cpu_overload or container_cpu_limit_too_low.

believed_cause: productcatalogservice ListProducts is likely repeatedly opening and reading /src/log.csv on every request, causing the CPU saturation and latency; the agent's claim that ListProducts creates /tmp/tmp.csv with 30000 rows is unsupported because the retrieved source excerpt ended at imports.
lesson: Never confirm a productcatalogservice file-write defect from a FILESYSTEM_WRITE_SURGE alert or an imports-only product_catalog.go excerpt; retrieve the full ListProducts body and default to the known repeated /src/log.csv read mechanism unless a write site is visibly present.
summary: Strengthened productcatalogservice source-evidence guardrails so an imports-only product_catalog.go excerpt or a filesystem-write surge cannot confirm code_excessive_file_writes; retrieve full ListProducts and prefer code_excessive_file_reads when repeated /src/log.csv reads are the visible mechanism.
